dimensions.explanation: The selected application concerns distributors promoting SFC-authorised funds to clients, including a specific product or a particular product type. Public advertising, online distribution and an actual investment are not stated prerequisites. The quoted Code wording may extend beyond funds, but that broader application is outside this selected application.

Distributors are identified, but gift and discount are not exhaustively defined. Guaranteed returns and other incentives may be gifts; their status is not automatic. Fund returns and distributor top-ups are distinct components.

The fee-or-charge discount exception attaches to the benefit classified as a discount. Its presence in a combined offer does not expressly exempt another gift component. Whether a rebate or top-up qualifies as a discount requires classification.

The operative wording is 'should not offer'; 'may be considered a gift' qualifies classification, not permission to offer a benefit already classified as a non-exempt gift. The proposed prohibition label represents this selected Code restriction, not a finding of a statutory offence.

The control concerns offering gifts during promotion and specifies no duration, threshold or commencement date. The 30 September 2010 date identifies referenced FAQ material, not an effective date established by this packet.

Gift assessment remains relevant when an arrangement is not a structured product. Section 103 authorisation or exemption is not stated to disapply paragraph 3.11. The full Code and referenced FAQ answer are not supplied, limiting resolution of classification questions.

questions: What criteria distinguish a gift from an underlying fund return, distributor top-up or other incentive in the particular arrangement?
Does the particular rebate or return reduce identifiable fees or charges, and which component qualifies for the discount exception?
What does the referenced FAQ answer say about product-type linkage and combined offers?
What applicable Code version and commencement provisions govern the assessed offer? Neither is established by this packet.

assumptions: The selected control is applied to one separately identified benefit component offered by one distributor to a client in a fund promotion.
Each component of a combined offer is assessed separately; a discount component does not transfer its exception to another component.
Gift status and discount status are supplied as reasoned classifications, not inferred solely from the label 'guaranteed return' or 'incentive'.
A product-type link is sufficient without naming one fund; actual investor distraction is not an additional prerequisite.
The formalization addresses the selected gift restriction only. It does not decide section 103 liability or overall compliance.

citations.quote: (i) the actual return of the relevant fund(s) invested by the investor (ie, fund return); and (ii) a top-up return to make up the difference between the fund return and the guaranteed rate of return offered by the distributor.
Even where the guaranteed returns offered would not constitute a “structured product” under the SFO
as they may be considered a gift that should not be offered to investors.
distributors should not offer any gifts (other than a discount of fees or charges) in promoting a specific investment product or a particular type of investment product to a client.

If gifts are offered in such a way that they are linked to a particular type of investment product, such as certain types of funds or funds offered by certain fund houses, then such gifts will be bound by this requirement
in breach of section 103 of the SFO or paragraph 3.11 of the Code of Conduct.

readings.distinction: This component-level reading preserves both the product-type reach and the narrow discount exception. A combined offer can contain an exempt discount and a separately restricted gift. It also preserves the classification qualification: an additional return is not automatically a gift. The strongest uncertainty is classification of economically mixed rebates or top-ups; the supplied text does not support a definite competing classification rule.

readings.statement: [TRUE_IS_PROHIBITED] For the selected paragraph 3.11 gift control, true means the assessed distributor offers this component to a client in a qualifying product or product-type promotion, the component is a gift, and it is not a discount of fees or charges. False means this component does not meet that selected restriction predicate; it does not establish overall compliance or exempt other components. Unknown classifications remain unknown. Apply the predicate separately to each component of a combined offer.
